entries.symbol: Startup move of action items and decisions to flat ids
entries.behavior: Once startup content settles, moves every stored action item and decision whose id has a colon ("board:<id>", "inbox:<source>:<entity>", "<conversation>:<type>:<n>:<hash>"), which directory sync stores as nested folders, to its flat id, keeping content, visibility and timestamps. A hand-added card is named after its title. A move that stopped after writing the flat id is finished on the next start.
entries.currentConsumers: Action items and decisions stored in deployed brains and their synced content repos before flat ids.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored action items or decisions with a colon in their id across supported upgrade sources.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before flat ids derives colon ids again, so it can take an Inbox item onto the board twice or re-add a conversation card the board already owns.

entries.behavior: Reads action items stored before the frontmatter trim: takes capturedAt from timeRange.end, flattens nested-identity people to { name, id, aliases }, and ignores spaceId, sourceSummaryId, sourceMessageCount and projectionVersion. The next write stores the trimmed shape.
entries.currentConsumers: Action items stored in deployed brains before the trim.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored action items carrying a retired field or a nested person across supported upgrade sources, or rewrite them in place.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before the trim reads only the old shape; items rewritten in the trimmed shape need the forward release.

entries.behavior: Preserves timestamp-only capture claims without automatically replaying them; new captures use atomic entity mutation receipts.
entries.currentConsumers: Persisted faq.captured-replies entries that cannot distinguish completed captures from interrupted attempts.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Explicitly reconcile all existing claims into verified durable dispositions or retire them with owner approval, and stop all old claim writers. Age alone cannot prove completion.
entries.rollbackDependency: Retain existing claims to avoid counting historical completed captures twice. New receipts are not understood by older runtimes; rolling back capture code requires disabling capture or a separately verified downgrade plan.

entries.behavior: Reads old topic fields and strips the retired Sources body section.
entries.currentConsumers: Topic markdown created before the canonical topic schema.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Rewrite supported topic stores to the canonical schema and observe zero old fields or Sources sections.
entries.rollbackDependency: Prior topic entities remain readable until the rewrite has passed its rollback window.

entries.behavior: Rejects removed token configuration with an actionable error.
entries.currentConsumers: Operators upgrading configurations that predate signed A2A trust.
entries.removalPrerequisite: The minimum supported upgrade source no longer documents or accepts either removed field.
entries.rollbackDependency: None; the fields are already rejected.

entries.behavior: Read-only checks recognize the current Changesets 2 prerelease state; a reviewed version operation exclusively moves consumed Markdown into the Changesets 3 archive and commits the new state last, rolling back ordinary failures.
entries.currentConsumers: The canonical repository's pre-transition pre.json and the parent Git revision used by release-mode classification during the first transition cycle.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Verify the first canonical Changesets 3 version transition and a subsequent release-mode cycle using only the new state shape; then remove the retired state fields and decoder branch.
entries.rollbackDependency: Failure rollback preserves the old state and source bytes. After a successful transition, a tooling downgrade requires a separately reviewed restoration of the old state and archived Markdown; the old CLI cannot consume the new metadata directly.
entries.targetRelease: post-Changesets-3-transition, after one verified release-mode cycle

entries.behavior: Converts retired model and preset configuration into explicit canonical bundles without booting a brain.
entries.currentConsumers: Users upgrading pre-unification brain.yaml files.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Stable 0.2.0 is published and the declared public migration-support window closes.
entries.rollbackDependency: No runtime rollback dependency; retained only for offline upgrades.

entries.behavior: Replaces a previously managed www CNAME when claiming the canonical alias.
entries.currentConsumers: Deployments whose DNS was provisioned by older deploy scripts.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Audit supported domains and confirm no managed www CNAME requires in-place replacement.
entries.rollbackDependency: The DNS record remains recoverable from provider history and prior deploy configuration.

entries.behavior: Stages retired model/preset or unversioned four-bundle pilot desired state as an isolated capability-bundle review copy, requiring reviewed source-to-target selections and explicit hosted package pins.
entries.currentConsumers: The one reviewed private-pilot capability-bundle crossover and its offline rollback preparation.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Phase 11 reaches zero-drift second reconcile and hosted canaries plus yeehaa.io soak one week on the unified alpha.
entries.rollbackDependency: Retained through the defined crossover rollback horizon; active ops loading never imports it.

entries.behavior: Parses persisted playbook runs that still carry the retired XState snapshot field.
entries.currentConsumers: Playbook runs written before event-sourced rehydration became canonical.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Migrate or expire all supported persisted snapshots and observe zero reads of the retired field.
entries.rollbackDependency: Old playbook runs remain readable during migration rollback.

entries.behavior: Recognizes generated starter identities from older releases before replacing placeholders.
entries.currentConsumers: Profiles initialized from supported pre-canonical starter content.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Backfill or preserve all supported starter profiles and observe zero matching old fingerprints.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older placeholder identities must remain distinguishable during rollback.

entries.behavior: Normalizes old generated deploy YAML before deciding whether a scaffold can be safely replaced.
entries.currentConsumers: Repositories upgrading standalone deploy artifacts generated by older brain releases.
entries.removalPrerequisite: All supported repositories have canonical deploy scaffolds and the old scaffold rollback window is closed.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older generated deploy files must remain recognizable during scaffold rollback.

entries.behavior: Accepts package-owned runtime plugin factories used by older internal site integrations.
entries.currentConsumers: Supported site packages that have not moved entirely to declarative composition.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Migrate all supported site packages and public declarations away from SitePackage.plugin.
entries.rollbackDependency: Prior site package versions require the factory while they remain supported rollback targets.

entries.behavior: Instantiates a first-party entity, service or interface package converted from a class under the plugin id its class had, so its template, data source, job and channel names stay those sites, brains and queued jobs use, and an interface keeps the daemon names it registered under that id (`cli:cli`), and a config the package refuses is reported under that id, as its class reported it; a package of several message interfaces keeps none, since each of them is its own plugin; a service that owns one type installs it under the type itself, as an entity plugin class was named after its type; and a converted service keeps the plugin dependencies its class declared, registering after them and not starting without them. Only the canonical brain's composer and a plugin eval's eval.yaml (`pluginId`) name it; package source never does.
entries.currentConsumers: First-party entity and service packages converted to declarative definitions and composed by the canonical brain, and their plugin evals (wishlist, decks, note, portfolio, blog, link, social-media), and a service owning its one type (playbooks, its type installed as playbook); onboarding's dependency on playbook and playbooks; and first-party interfaces converted to declarative definitions, under their class plugin ids: the terminal (chat-repl, `cli`), which the app registers with --cli, Email (`email`), MCP (`mcp`, its protocol-only registration under the same id), A2A (`a2a`), chat (`chat`) and web chat (`web-chat`).
entries.removalPrerequisite: Decide whether first-party packages adopt package-scoped names; if they do, migrate site template references, brain configs and queued job types to the scoped names.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release with class plugins reads the same plugin, template, data source and job names.

entries.behavior: Gives a first-party entity definition internal capabilities bound to the create route, eval, data source fetch, contract job, declared job or generation it was handed: nearest records by embedding distance at the call's visibility, a free-form structured AI answer, generation through a template the declaring type declares (in the brain's voice when asked), reads of the package's own types at every visibility, read-only untyped reads of every type at the call's scope (a data source fetch's build scope, a create route's public scope, a contract job's run, a declared job's or generation's run, read as its requester or as the package that queued it), the package's logger and the anchor's profile, as the entity plugin classes' handlers had them, a generation's result marked to land under the next free id when its own is taken, as the classes' generations created with deduplicateId, a create route's hand-off to the ordinary create (with the target it resolved), its pending placeholder with a queued contract job (reused, or written under the next free id with the job's input built from the placeholder as stored, with or without a link, attributed to the caller as content work or as data processing routed to their channel), and its complete record under the next free id; contract jobs (`contractJob`), which other packages queue by their contract's type with the input as written and which run as the package (one may answer the type's generation job name when the type declares no generation, for jobs an entity plugin class queued under it), with the image model, attachment resolution, the shared upload store, and links into a target under the generation-link rules and its visibility, past its action policy, as the entity plugin classes' job handlers wrote them; answers to first-party contracts under the channels they already have (`answering(definition, [entityAnswer(contract, handle, { everyProcess? })])`), given the request, the sender and the declaring type's reads and writes as the package, released with the package; the caller of a create route or its check (`entityRuntime(context).caller`: interface, signed-in user, channel), as the classes' interceptors read their execution context; a create route for a URL alone (`withUrlRoute(definition, route)`), as system_create hands a URL source on and the link class captured it; writes that keep the frontmatter order of the document they replace (`writesInDocumentOrder(definition)`), for types whose files people write by hand, as the classes' adapters wrote over existing frontmatter; a publish provider built with the plugin's logger when it is handed to the publish pipeline (`loggedProvider(name, build)`), as the classes built their clients with a child of their own logger; an eval's run of its type's own generation (`entityRuntime(evalContext).runGeneration(input, { onProgress })`), in process and as the package, writing the record and answering the job's result, as the classes' evals ran their generation handlers; a step after a generation runs (`afterGeneration(generation, step)`), told the id and title it wrote or why it failed, with its input and the package's jobs and retry scope, as the classes' generation handlers queued follow-up work; the entity-text helpers; `ensureUniqueTitle` with `uniqueTitleContext(runtime)`, the classes' free-title check read through a call's runtime; a body template the vault scaffolds a new record with (`withBodyTemplate(definition, template)`), as the classes' body formatters gave one; metadata stored as the document a type wrote states it (`restatingMetadata(definition, restate)`), so a slug resolved on the first write is the file's own from then on, as the classes' adapters read it back; and the template builder and record schemas a definition's rendered templates use. The public context types never name them; a context the runtime did not build is refused.
entries.currentConsumers: First-party entity packages converted to declarative definitions whose create routes or evals need search, structured checks or package-wide placement (wishlist, doc), whose data sources read across types (series), or whose jobs other packages queue by contract and whose routes queue them (image, document), or whose create routes describe through their templates and whose generations check that their title is free and deduplicate their id, and whose resolved slug is stated once stored (decks), or that answer a first-party contract and import an upload through a contract job queued from the placeholder they wrote (note), or whose create routes describe through their templates, whose body has sections the vault scaffolds and whose resolved slug is stated once stored (portfolio), or whose generations read their sources, series and the anchor's name at the run's scope and whose resolved slug is stated once stored (blog), or whose links are captured from the URL a request names, as the caller's data processing in their channel, by contract jobs that extract through its template under both its capture and its generation job names, and whose hand-written files keep their order (link), or whose generations ask again for a taken title, read their sources at the run's scope and queue a graphic once written, whose evals run their own generation, and whose LinkedIn provider is built with the plugin's logger (social-media), or whose hand-written files keep their order (playbook).
entries.removalPrerequisite: Promote each capability to the public entity contract once a third-party package needs it, or retire it when no first-party package does.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: the capabilities are bound per call and store nothing.

entries.behavior: Gives a first-party service converted from a class what the public service contract does not offer: tools whose local names keep the underscore their class gave them (`atproto-registry_check_contracts`), which the public `defineTool` refuses, or the bare name their class registered them under (`playbook_manage`, `inbox_list`), unprefixed; and, through `serviceRuntime(context)` on its subscriptions, tools, dashboardWidgets and studioWorkspaces slot contexts, answers to first-party contracts under the channels they already have (`notifications:send`), in job workers too with `everyProcess`, including one every owner answers and the asker gathers (`agent:context:request`), system and broadcast channels heard as the class subscribed, observed or heard them in every process, each with the sender the bus stamped on it, the package's logger, the delivery provider registered for a channel type, handlers run once the brain is ready, where the class's onReady ran, handlers run once every plugin has registered, in every process, where its onRegistrationComplete ran (a failure fails registration), the shape of every registered entity type (its frontmatter schema, whether it is a singleton, its body template), the brain's data directory, and the brain's character, its anchor's profile and its domain as the shell keeps them, read-only reads of the entity service (types, counts, a page, one record, a search) at the scope each call names, the auth backend the brain bound, read when asked, the Inbox sources other plugins registered and the follow-ups their destinations resolve, read-only, a recurring check under the plugin's id in every process, a way into the brain (never from a worker), the URL Studio serves one of its workspaces at, the brain's site URL, the route a well-known role names, the running tool call's conversation and caller permission level, and the runtime state its class stored under the namespace the class named (`playbooks.runs`), eval handlers under the plugin's id (`playbooks:goalCheck`), none in a worker, Studio for a workspace it composes from declared ones (each built under the plugin's id as a source and never registered on its own, the composed one registered once, never in a worker, as the class registered it), and a claim on a shell system type (anchor-profile, brain-character): its stored records read and written as the package, past the action policy and with expectedContentHash honored, its frontmatter extension and persist validator, one package per type, refused for a type a plugin registers or nobody registered, the brain's profile-kind catalog, one structured answer from the brain's AI and a bounded verdict from its judge, and a data source, a built template and a self-drawing Dashboard widget under the plugin's id, reading the corpus (lists, counts, nearest records, the semantic projection) at the build's or the viewer's scope; and, through `withOwnedDataSources(definition, dataSources)`, data sources installed on the types its header owns, scoped and read as an entity package's are, as its entity plugin class registered them (`site-info:entities`). Answers, channels and ready handlers act as the package and are released when it shuts down; a context the runtime did not build is refused.
entries.currentConsumers: First-party service packages converted to declarative definitions whose class tools were named in snake case (atproto-registry), or that answer first-party contracts and hear system channels as their classes did (notifications), or render every entity type once the brain is ready (obsidian-vault), or seed through another package's steward and register a starter as their classes did (onboarding), or answer for the site's metadata in every process with their type's data source as their entity plugin class did (site-info), or extend, validate and keep the shell's identity types as their class did (profile), or serve a map of the corpus to sites and the Dashboard (knowledge-map), or compose a Studio workspace from declared tabs and administer the brain's people through its auth backend (admin), or read the Inbox, register a recurring digest and a way in, and keep bare tool names and read the tool call (unified-inbox), or keep their class's runtime state, eval handler, bare tool name and gathered answer, judge a goal against the brain and hear who sent a conversation's messages (playbooks).
entries.removalPrerequisite: Rename the snake-case tools to kebab case, with their evals, docs and agent instructions, or promote the underscore to the public tool-name rule; move first-party contracts to owner-named channels or promote cross-process answers and system-channel listening to the public service contract once a third-party package needs them.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: tool names, answers and subscriptions are registered per run and store nothing.

entries.behavior: Gives a first-party interface converted from a class what the public interface contract does not offer. Through `interfaceRuntime(context)` on its setup, routes and daemons contexts and on its first-party slots: the interface's logger; the brain's agent, a turn in a conversation and the answer to an approval it waits on, as the class reached them through context.agent; a conversation's stored messages; whether a sender stands for the brain's anchor; and, for an interface with a message transport only, the message coordination its class inherited (the input it is answering, which holds job completions back until the reply is out, and job progress a terminal UI follows); answers to first-party contracts under the channels they already have (`email:source-read`), with the sender, released when the interface shuts down; requests to another package's contract; the runtime state its class stored under the namespace the class named (`email.inbound.uid-cursor`); a sender's permission level on an interface; whether the brain runs in production, its domain and whether a plugin is registered; the auth backend the brain bound, read when asked; the brain's MCP service for a protocol transport; its endpoint and its way into the brain; a typed channel it hears in the main process, released at shutdown; handlers run once the brain is ready, where the class's onReady ran; the brain's character and anchor profile, its resolved profile kind, its public skills and the tools a permission level may call; read-only entity reads (whether a type is registered, a page, one record) at the scope each call names; the runtime's shared upload store (`upload`, at the route the interface names) and the retirement of a retired upload namespace's directory (nothing beside it, never the shared store); gathered answers to a collect contract; the brain's shared spaces, site URL, local site URL and whether links prefer it; conversations started and messages added for a platform's shared space; whether guest turns can run, the brain's app info, theme stylesheet and preview URL, the route a well-known role names, an operational health check under the interface, an Inbox source, a job's status, and Studio for a workspace it composes from a declared one (never from a worker), shared with the first-party service runtime; conversations read, listed, renamed and deleted as the class did; and, with a message transport, the reply it tracks for a job and the tool completions a reply settles. Beside a public `defineInterface` definition, as plain data and functions: `withDaemon(definition, slot)`, a daemon its class registered, started and stopped under `<plugin id>:<id>` with its own health and no readiness to wait for (`cli:cli`), or none when the slot returns none; `withChannels(definition, slot)`, the channels its class registered, each descriptor as written (subject pattern, manual delivery) with its delivery when it declares one, in the worker as in the main process, which makes the interface a message interface as its class was; `withWebRoutes(definition, slot)`, the HTTP routes its class served as written (any response, with its public, preview, role and match settings), served once it registers after the routes its definition declares; `withTools(definition, slot)`, the tools its class registered under their names as written with their visibility, side effects and MCP exposure; `withProtocolPlugin(definition, protocol, config)`, a protocol-only registration of itself (another definition under the same plugin id and package, configured from the host's config) that the eval harness builds; and `withMessageTransport(definition, slot)`, which runs the runtime's message coordination for the interface and sends job progress and completions through the transport the slot returns, as its class extended the message interface base: rendering progress and completions, sending with an id and editing in place, and routing progress and tool events and the settling of held tool completions through hooks around the runtime's own handling. A context the runtime did not build is refused, a daemon id declared twice is refused, a transport, channels, web routes, tools and a protocol plugin are each declared once, and a definition defineInterface did not return is refused.
entries.currentConsumers: First-party interfaces converted to declarative definitions: the terminal (chat-repl), which answers through the agent with its own conversation and approvals, runs its Ink UI in a class-shaped daemon and shows job progress and completions through a message transport; Email, which registers the email channel with its subject pattern and, when configured, its Resend sender in every process, runs its IMAP listener as its class's daemon only with a mailbox, answers email:source-read, asks inbound-email and auth-principal-resolve, and keeps its IMAP cursor and source locators under its class's namespaces; MCP, which serves /status and /mcp through its own streamable HTTP transport, registers its chat and confirm tools under those names, builds its protocol-only registration for the eval harness, runs its server as mcp:mcp, advertises its endpoint and way in over HTTP, and reads the brain's production flag, domain, plugins, auth backend, MCP service, permission levels and job progress; A2A, which serves its Agent Card (ready once the brain is), agent directory and JSON-RPC endpoint with CORS and SSE on the shared webserver, registers agent_call, answers a2a:ask:request, a2a:call:request and a2a:call:agents, signs and verifies peer requests through the auth backend, keeps its public-ask allowance under a2a.public-asks, and reads the brain's identity, profile kind, public skills, public tools and saved agents; chat, which runs one Chat SDK app for Discord and Slack as chat:chat, registers both platforms' channels in every process, serves their webhooks, keeps uploads in the shared store and deletes its retired discord-chat and slack-chat upload directories once at startup, answers chat:space-notice, gathers space-notice actions, records shared-space conversations, keeps its thread subscriptions under its class's namespaces, and renders, edits and routes job progress and tool statuses through its message transport; web chat, which serves its Ask page, chat API, Ask assets and guest API on the shared host as written, streams replies, job progress and tool statuses to the browser through its message transport, keeps uploads in the shared store at its API path, runs web-chat:guest-maintenance from the scheduler, marks guest chat open once guest turns can run, records its guest state and Ask box availability under its class's namespaces, reports the guest usage record's health, and registers its guest monitor in Studio once the brain is ready.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Promote each capability to the public interface contract once a third-party interface needs it, or retire it when no first-party interface does.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: the capabilities are bound per registration and store nothing.

entries.behavior: Renders the older analytics script field when no registered head script replaces it.
entries.currentConsumers: Site configurations created before headScripts registration.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Migrate supported site configurations and observe zero use of the analytics script field.
entries.rollbackDependency: Old site configurations continue rendering during their support window.

entries.behavior: Loads the TypeScript eval configuration format when canonical brain.eval.yaml is absent.
entries.currentConsumers: External evaluation projects that still use defineConfig in brain.eval.config.ts.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Publish migration guidance and require brain.eval.yaml in the minimum supported evaluation project version.
entries.rollbackDependency: Old evaluation projects remain runnable during the migration window.

entries.behavior: Reads older message metadata and restricts messages that lack provenance.
entries.currentConsumers: Persisted conversations written before provenance metadata became mandatory.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Backfill supported conversations and observe zero messages without canonical provenance.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older conversations remain safely readable during rollback.

entries.behavior: Rejects retired model, preset, or implicit bundle configuration with migration guidance.
entries.currentConsumers: Users attempting to boot pre-unification configuration.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Stable 0.2.0 ships and public brain config migration support is removed.
entries.rollbackDependency: None; retired configuration is not accepted by the canonical runtime.

entries.behavior: Normalizes null or malformed metadata from older stored messages.
entries.currentConsumers: Persisted conversation rows created before metadata was always an object.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Backfill supported conversation databases and observe zero null or malformed metadata rows.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older rows remain readable during database rollback.

entries.behavior: Retains the Drizzle schema needed to migrate databases created by the former vector layout.
entries.currentConsumers: Entity database migrations from supported older releases.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Squash the entity migration baseline after the minimum supported upgrade source contains the replacement schema.
entries.rollbackDependency: Old entity databases require this migration schema during rollback and re-upgrade.

entries.behavior: Runs a declared {type}:generation job whose queued data is the entity plugin class handler's raw input (with the entity it fills beside it) rather than the runtime's package-job envelope: the input is checked by the generation's schema and the job runs as the package, since no requester was recorded. Data that names a requester is held to the envelope.
entries.currentConsumers: Generation jobs of the publishing entities (post, deck, project, social-post, link, note) queued by their class plugins before the conversion and still pending or retrying at upgrade.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Phase 2 close-out (slice 10): observe zero pending or retrying {type}:generation rows in the raw shape on supported runtime databases.
entries.rollbackDependency: None: a rolled-back class handler reads the raw shape it wrote.

entries.behavior: Atomically retires one explicitly selected pre-scheduler projection job only when it has no attempt ownership, progress, or result.
entries.currentConsumers: Rover databases that retained active projection rows after their job handlers moved to scheduler-owned projection rules.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Audit supported runtime databases and observe zero active skill:project, topic:project, swot:derive, or conversation-memory:project rows through the rollback window.
entries.rollbackDependency: Retained alpha rollback targets can still expose the pre-scheduler rows that block an idle predeploy snapshot.

entries.behavior: Supplies a fallback lease duration for direct dequeue callers that do not pass worker-owned lease settings.
entries.currentConsumers: Supported direct job-queue consumers outside the canonical worker claim path.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Require explicit lease settings on every supported dequeue caller and observe zero fallback use.
entries.rollbackDependency: Older direct dequeue callers require the fallback while they remain supported.

entries.behavior: Allows registered asset-backed entity types to retain inline binary content while mixed legacy/reference image migration is resumable.
entries.currentConsumers: Existing image rows that still contain data URLs during the image cutover and rollback window.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Verify every completed image stores a valid asset reference and legacy materialization telemetry remains at zero through the migration soak.
entries.rollbackDependency: The transitional release must read and update pre-migration image rows while the pre-cutover database remains the rollback source.

entries.symbol: frontmatterSchema scalar grammar, colon-string quoting, and binary representation
entries.behavior: Retains YAML 3 frontmatter octal/base-60 numeric meanings, colon-string quoting required by publishing consumers, and binary value representation while using the maintained YAML 4 parser; no executable engines or removed-API fallback.
entries.currentConsumers: Durable and custom frontmatter authored under gray-matter's YAML 3 schema, including external supported content sources.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Approve a durable-frontmatter format migration, verify equivalent values across supported content sources and rollback targets, and observe zero dependence on the previous scalar grammar.
entries.rollbackDependency: Removing the schema without that migration reinterprets bare values such as 012, 0o12, and 12:34 in existing documents.

entries.symbol: FAQ body read path from before the structured content formatter
entries.behavior: Reads FAQ bodies stored with the answer at the top and alternatives as ### sections under "## Alternative answers", FAQ sources stored in frontmatter, and source excerpts kept as "> " quote lines under each source. The next write stores the formatter layout with sources in the body and no quotes.
entries.currentConsumers: FAQs captured in deployed brains before the formatter layout, and their synced files.
entries.removalPrerequisite: Observe zero stored FAQs without an "## Answer" section, with frontmatter sources or with quoted sources across supported upgrade sources, or rewrite them in place.
entries.rollbackDependency: A brain rolled back to a release before the formatter layout cannot read FAQs rewritten in it; they need the forward release.

exemptions.reason: typescript-legacy is an npm alias used to isolate the compatibility compiler; it is not a persisted or runtime legacy contract.
pdfjs-dist/legacy is an upstream package export path and cannot be renamed locally.
deprecated is dependency-cruiser's dependency type for npm packages their authors deprecated; the rule forbids depending on them.
deprecated is the npm registry's version metadata field; the script verifies that retired packages carry it.
deprecated and deprecatedBy are lifecycle values of published ATProto lexicon metadata; they describe a lexicon's status, not compatibility code here.
